newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called to open flat to higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called to open flat to higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures are expected to open flat to higher Monday after ending lower Friday on weaker physical power prices and expected return of several power units from recent outages.

"It's slightly firmer especially COB (California-Oregon Border)," said an East Coast electricity dealer, attributing the early strength as a mild technical recovery rather than reaction to any bullish fundamental news.

In over-the-counter activity, June COB futures were quoted at $16.25-16.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Friday's settlement of $16.10, and June Palo Verde (PV) at $22.00-22.25 against Friday's close of $22.10.
More spot power supply this week will likely pressure physical electricity prices lower, market sources said.
Late Friday, the board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council announced it endorsed to increase the energy flow on the Pacific Intertie from 6,250 megawatts (MW) to 7,200 MW.

The transmission system, a major conduit in moving cheap hydropower from the Pacific Northwest to southern California, has been running below its maximum capacity of 7,900 MW after two major blackouts in the West last summer.
Bonneville Power Administration said it hopes to begin ramping up capacity on the intertie at midnight.

Several generating units were expected to come back up since this past weekend, including a 550 MW unit at Jim Bridger, a 750 MW unit at Four Corners, an 875 MW unit at the Intermountain plant and a 350 MW unit at the San Juan plant.
Weakness in natural gas futures could also put downward pressure on the complex, market sources said.
NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas futures fell 1.2 cent to $2.230 per million British thermal units in early trading.

The western half of the country would generally be warm and dry for the next several days with the exception of the mountainous region in the Southwest where there is chance of scattered thunderstorms.

In the Northwest, temperatures in cities like Portland and Seatttle are expected to hit the mid-70s to mid-80s F. In the Southwest, readings along the coast are projected to run in the 70s-80s, while those in the interior desert area would likely hit the 100s.
